dream_dotted_colossus.name: Dream Body — dotted colossus
dream_dotted_colossus.description: The dotted colossus family, grown from a seed and varied along cladding (dots, marble, brick, fur, drape) and stance (contrapposto, torsion, fragment, pair, frieze).

predicted_degeneracy.reasoning: silhouette budget for one figure, in square metres of projected area: torso 0.24, legs 0.24, arms 0.12, head 0.05 = 0.65 total. Torsion moves the crossing arm to the far shoulder — 0.06 vacated plus 0.06 arrived, but half the arrival lands ON the chest and is not new pixels, so ~0.09; the other arm goes behind the back, ~0.04 net; the head turns 45 deg and repaints ~40% of 0.05 = 0.02; the counter-rotated shoulder and hip move the torso edge ~20 mm over 0.6 m = 0.012. Sum 0.162 of 0.65 = 25% of the SILHOUETTE. At framing 0.62 a 1.6 m body is about 26% of the frame, so 0.25 x 0.26 = 6.4% of picture. Every other stance pair adds or removes a whole body, a head and two arms, or a 0.72 m column, and every cladding pair repaints the entire surface.
predicted_degeneracy.outcome: RIGHT PAIR, WRONG AXIS, AND THE ARITHMETIC WAS RIGHT TWICE BY ACCIDENT. contrapposto-vs-torsion is the smallest stance pair in all five claddings (6.07 dots, 7.59 fur, 8.49 drape, 9.71 brick, 9.90 marble, mean 8.35), so the pair was named correctly and 6.4 predicted against 6.07 measured is 0.95x — under the prediction, which by the corpus's rule means stop and look. Looking says the two errors cancelled: the subject is 15.1% of frame, not the 26% assumed, and the silhouette share is nearer 40% than the 25% computed. WHAT THE PREDICTION MISSED is that the gallery's minimum is on the OTHER axis — marble-vs-brick at 2.275%, stance=fragment, smallest of all 300 pairs and one of three under the 3% decoration line. The clause 'every cladding pair repaints the entire surface' was the false step. Two causes, and only the second one is real: the cape was built on the +Z hemisphere (the reference is shot from behind) while the sweep camera stands at yaw 0.62 in front, so it now wraps 2.2 rad and over both deltoids — worth 0.1 points, i.e. NOTHING, which is how the standpoint theory was disproved. The real cause is the DENOMINATOR: a cape over the back of a body that is itself 15% of frame is ~2% of picture whatever it is made of, and pale brick on pale marble spends little value on top of that. It is faithful to the reference and small in the frame at once, and the frame is not the argument. Kept, and recorded, rather than tuned until the number flattered it.
